entries.security_assessment: REJECTED on review. The repo's own README calls it a 'demo app... not intended to be used in production.' By default it sends full session transcripts -- user messages, assistant responses, thinking blocks, tool usage, so any secrets/code/output that appeared in a session -- to a cloud Letta server, with no stated redaction/retention/encryption policy. Requires a separate LETTA_API_KEY. 'Full' SDK-tools mode grants it Bash/Edit/Write/Task, letting it modify files and spawn subagents on its own. One memory agent serves all projects by default, so one repo's data can leak context into another.

entries.name: earshot (name collision -- multiple unrelated projects)
entries.category: Claude MCP server / plugin (ambiguous which one is wanted)
entries.description: Ambiguous name: at least 4 distinct, unrelated repos share it -- (1) Leonxlnx/earshot, a local CPU-only MIT-licensed MCP server that turns audio into structured, reasoning-over-able data (spectrograms, loudness, sound-effect maps, speech transcription) -- best match for 'gives Claude ears'; (2) mromanczuk/earshot, a macOS-only plugin that speaks Claude Code's turn summaries/prompts aloud; (3) shreyashguptas/earshot, reads Claude Code's last response aloud via /tldr; (4) a separate AirPods/head-gesture voice-control project, same name.

entries.security_assessment: SkillSpector scan (--no-llm): score 11/100, severity LOW, recommendation CAUTION -- 3 MEDIUM findings (External Transmission, 50% confidence) at hooks/route.ts:57,59 and tests/switchboard.test.tsx:93. Manually reviewed: route.ts sends only the subagent type and a short task label to one of three external classifier APIs (TypeSafe/Vercel AI Gateway/OpenAI, user-configured) to pick the model -- the source's own comment states the full task text (which can hold code/paths/hostnames/keys) is deliberately never sent. Real external data transmission by design, not a leak; needs the user's own API key for the chosen picker to function at all.

Install path is a curl|sh / iwr|iex shell installer (macOS/Linux and Windows variants) -- review before running, standard caution for any piped installer. Requires a Kaggle account's API credentials: the safe path is ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json (chmod 600, per the project's own docs), NOT the authenticate() tool's inline-key option, which would put the API key in the chat transcript.
